subject: Ownership of partial uptime hit during transit outage
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: BrightStack Ops <ops@brightstack.com>; Nadia Ruiz <nadia@brightstack.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Ownership of partial uptime hit during transit outage

Hi Nadia / BrightStack Ops team,

We observed a 12-minute partial degradation on 2027-04-09 that our uptime ledger categorized as a partial availability hit. Our initial tally marks 00:12 of degraded service between 03:24 and 03:36 UTC. BrightStack reported an upstream transit provider blip — we need to resolve whether that event is excluded as BrightStack maintenance or counted against Redwood SLOs.

Why this matters: the customer (BrightStack trial account BS-ENTER-0012) is in a renewal window and wants clarity on whether this incident reduces our uptime calculations for April. The customer is asking for a formal apportionment explanation and any credits.

Requests:
- Full packet/flow-level evidence or probe traces showing when traffic dropped and whether it correlates with BrightStack's maintenance windows.
- Any carrier incident IDs and timelines (ingress point, ASN info).
- Your position on ownership (BrightStack upstream vs. Redwood network) and any suggested split if responsibility is shared.

I've attached our SLO window screenshot showing how the 12 minutes was counted for reference. Marcus, can you confirm the probe correlation we saw from our east-us and eu-west collectors? Lauren, looping you for commercial visibility.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Accounts Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-slo-screenshot.png
From: Nadia Ruiz <nadia@brightstack.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>, BrightStack Ops <ops@brightstack.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Ownership of partial uptime hit during transit outage

Jonas — thanks for the quick ping.

Summary: Our infra team traced the impact to a transit provider (AS64499) that reported a 00:18 outage window starting 03:22 UTC; BrightStack did not schedule maintenance at that time. We are sharing our incident summary and the transit provider log; see attachments. On our side there were no config changes or scheduled maintenance that overlap that window.

Attachments included:
- bstack-incident-summary.pdf (internal timeline and ticket IDs)
- transit-outage-log.csv (carrier incident timestamps and AS path samples)

We believe the event is attributable to the transit provider and not BrightStack maintenance, but we acknowledge some of the degraded flows traversed Redwood egress nodes and that may have amplified the customer experience. We're open to a pragmatic split if Redwood's evidence shows the degraded period inside your SLO window was materially extended by edge-level routing.

For next steps: our ops lead can share 1:1 traceroutes and flow logs for the affected prefixes if that helps expedite reconciliation.

—Nadia Ruiz
Head of Customer Operations
BrightStack
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>
To: Nadia Ruiz <nadia@brightstack.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Ownership of partial uptime hit during transit outage

Nadia — thanks for the context and the files. Marcus and I reviewed the carrier CSV against our probe data. A few notes and an initial proposal: 

Observations:
- Our probes show degraded request latencies (increase > 500ms and 10% error spikes) from 03:23:45 to 03:36:05 UTC — that aligns with your 03:22–03:40 window but ours extends ~1m25s longer.
- The majority of failing traces show the path shift was through BrightStack's upstream ASN; however, some percentage (approx. 18%) of failed connections terminated after hitting Redwood egress and failed to reconnect cleanly.

Given the overlap, Redwood proposes a pragmatic derate split: BrightStack 60% responsibility / Redwood 40% responsibility for the counted 12 minutes. That would translate into a proportional credit against the month for BS-ENTER-0012 rather than a full-customer credit.

Evidence we need to finalize:
- 1:1 traceroutes for a sample of 20 failing flows (you offered) with timestamps and AS path.
- Any carrier incident ID that ties the 03:22 start to their reported outage.

Commercial note (Lauren): if BrightStack is not willing to accept a split, we may need to escalate for a formal SLA dispute with legal sign-off. Our preference is to resolve operationally.

Marcus, attaching the probe correlation file we used (summary row included). Nadia, if you can send the traceroute samples and a short statement from your transit provider that would close the loop.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachments: redwood-slo-screenshot.png
From: BrightStack Ops <ops@brightstack.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodai.com>, Nadia Ruiz <nadia@brightstack.com>, accounts@brightstack.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Ownership of partial uptime hit during transit outage

Jonas / Lauren / Marcus — following internal review and a call with the transit provider, BrightStack will accept shared responsibility for the customer impact. The carrier provided incident ID TP-4427 and timestamps that match our earlier summary; however, the carrier acknowledged a transient annealing in their routing that caused reordering and timeouts which interacted poorly with Redwood's egress retries. 

Outcome proposal:
- BrightStack accepts 60% of the responsibility; Redwood accepts 40% as proposed.
- For BS-ENTER-0012 we will apply a single proportional service credit equal to 60% of the calculated downtime credit value. Redwood to apply the 40% portion on your billing side; BrightStack will handle the 60% via our account team.
- We'll attach a short joint statement for the customer and close the ticket once both sides confirm the wording.

Next steps:
1) Nadia to share the 20 traceroute samples and carrier confirmation (they will be added to the incident folder).
2) Accounts to issue/record the proportional credit (accounts@brightstack.com) and provide a DocuSign acknowledgement if needed: https://www.docusign.com/links/abc123
3) Redwood to send the proposed joint statement for customer-facing language by EOD Thu, Apr 15.

Thanks — appreciate the constructive approach. If either side needs a formal SLA review, ping Lauren and we'll route to legal.

—BrightStack Ops

Attachments referenced: transit-outage-log.csv, bstack-incident-summary.pdf
